owned_question: Can a real platform-specific optional dependency update be target-relevant while the inspected standard and platform test workflows remain non-discriminating because they do not install the affected extra?
established: PR #34 changes NumPy only inside the mlx optional dependency group.
The mlx extra is an exact-pinned Apple-Silicon runtime family.
The target contains a real MLXWhisperEngine that imports mlx, mlx_whisper and NumPy.
The engine-selection path requires hardware acceleration and is_mlx_available().
is_mlx_available() requires macOS arm64 and an installed/discoverable mlx_whisper package.
The target's Apple-Silicon development instructions explicitly install --extra mlx.
The standard PR test/typecheck workflow installs only .[dev].
The dedicated macOS test workflow installs only .[dev].
Therefore those inspected workflows do not form the optional dependency environment changed by the PR.
not_established: NumPy 2.4.6 is incompatible with Dictare's MLX stack.
All repository workflows omit the mlx extra.
A particular PR run was green.
Every Apple-Silicon user activates MLX regardless of configuration.
The coordinated family cannot be updated independently under any circumstances.
durable_distinctions: dependency declared != dependency installed in the observed environment
matching platform workflow != affected optional dependency environment formed
optional dependency installed != runtime backend necessarily selected
workflow success != evidence for a dependency path the workflow never forms

stop_reason.label: optional_activation_and_ci_boundary_resolved
stop_reason.explanation: Exact static repository evidence is sufficient to establish the conditional MLX activation path and the non-coverage of the two inspected test workflows. Running Apple-Silicon hardware or NumPy 2.4.6 would answer a different compatibility question.

future_evaluation_value: avoid treating platform match as runtime-path coverage
